Troubleshooting for unsuccessful key programming 

1. Ask tech what kind of "error message" he gets or at what step he is stuck. 

2. Confirm YMM by VIN and verify that you are using the correct part. Maybe split year? 
 
3. Jumper cable connected? Is the car battery good? if not connected, connect and retry

4. If you have the option and it's doable, try a different key. (maybe defective part)

5. Double-check again DB and ensure you are trying to program a key that is possible to program with the current tool you are using. 

6. Have tech investigate if there could be anything unusual going on with the car, for example: when was used last time, auction car?, didn't use it for several years/months, replaced an electronic part like ECU, etc...

7. Notify Santi or Matt and ask for assistance. (When you do so, provide all the info you checked in the steps before)

No more than 5 seconds between each step from now on

• IGN ON
• 1 sec press on LOCK
• IGN OFF 
5. Do this 1 times 
• IGN ON
• 1 sec press on LOCK
• KEEP IGNITION ON 

6. Door locks will cycle 
7. Press LOCK one last time. 
8. IGN OFF - Done

Pick one space up one space down etc.. (if you sense a tumbler down with one arm, the second arm will sense a tumbler down as well, both arms basically sense tumblers in the same direction - never opposite)

Lishi has 2 arms.

One pointer up
One pointer down 
Each pointer is marked A or B

Lock contains:
5 spaces (1-5)
6 depths (1-6)

Spaces: 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 - 5
Track A: A - A - A - A - A
Track B: B - B - B - B - B 

In spaces 1 and 5 you will only be able to read 1 depth (either for A or B track)
 
In spaces 2-4 you will be able to read both A and B track depths.

Key won’t go pass acc. 

That points out at an issue with the switch and not with the core. 

Remove to plastic cover. Pops out. 

Remove 2 torx screws each side of wheel by tilting wheel for access using a key. 

Unsnap top cover completely at the connection with the cluster. 

Remove 3rd torx under bottom plastic. 
Remove bottom cover. 

Work now GENTLY. 
Remove plastic cover for PCB board like KVM style has mainly easy clips and one tiny torx on top - tilt wheel to access it. 

Pull down PCB board, undo 2 big plugs and one more small plug. Set aside super carefully as it can’t bend some pins on it. 

Identify bottom edge of left headless bolt. Drill a tiny hole in it and hit-twist it with hammer and straight pick. 

When easily spins finish removing it from the top by pressing down on the headless part and twisting with a flat head. 

Now the right bolt... poke small hole with drill on it, use same hit & twist method, that’s the hardest parts in the job. 

Bolt out - pull down hard on ignition to free it up, disconnect one more small plug (don’t forget to return that one when re-installing).

Remove plastics from customers housing and put on the new housing, see images. 

Put ignition ON if you can press pin and remove it and put it on new housing. 

If can’t turn ignition ON destroy the ignition switch completely and get it out in pieces, now ignition turns. 

Test customer’s ignition in the new housing. 

Re-install everything in the car.
Make & program key if needed.

get 10 mm socket.

Free this black plastic cover from 1 white harness it’s attached to, use a flat head. 

You may need to peel away the carpet a little for next step: 

Take a good picture of about 8 FEM harnesses. Remove FEM’s bottom red 12V harness first by 

pulling outward on red tab first

Now connect FEM cable blue alligator to FEM’s 12V power entry, then FEM cable OBD port goes to VVDI OBD. Blue light will turn on FEM cable. 
That’s it rest of the plugs aren’t used.

Locate 8 leg device by corner by an MCU.

Remove FEM cable

“Step #2 will start… load eeprom…”
Ok

VVDI Prog 
Load the new “service mode” file
Write on the 8 leg, verify 

VVDI2
Connect FEM cable with 12V to FEM

Proceed to step #3 “programming” on the bench. (Updating system, takes a few min)
Confirm 12V to FEM
“Yes” to continue 

Then proceed to step #4: writing back original EEPROM to 8 leg. 

Reinstall FEM go to car.

Now go step #5 “restore coding” only in the car after reinstalling fem. On bench won’t work. It’ll have you load coding file.

Yes
“SUCCESS….” :) ok

“This unit no need programming..”

Select “have working key”
Next

Ok

12 down

WRITE what you read in pairs

A   BA  BA   BA  BA   BA  B
2   43   22   13   44   12   3

column1: 2014 Jeep Patriot - Repair it replace ignition cylinder.
column16:
2014 Jeep Patriot - Repair it replace ignition cylinder. 

Better to disconnect negative battery terminal. 

Remove bottom three torx screws on lower cover

Remove windshield wiper by taking the phillips screw out on the vertical side facing the passenger door and slide it out of the holder. 

You may need to remove the wire connector (not a must). 

Removal of the windshield wiper module will expose the torx screw for the black plastic Immo module. Remove it.

Unplug the two connectors to the immobilizer.

CAREFULLY push out the three clips around the ignition key cylinder housing on the anti theft modules black ring.

The hole is now visible from the top of the steering column.

Use light to illuminate the hole. turn the ignition to acc or on and push the ignition all the way in. This should expose the release pin on the cylinder. 

Insert a small pick into the hole to depress the release pin. Gently pull on the cylinder while slowy removing the small pick from the hole.

The cylinder should come out.

2005 Ford Escape - ignition replacement. Ford Focus Ignition works, but isn’t the correct exact part because those ignition also have a facecap to grab onto. 

Plastics removed by removing 3 philips screws. 

Ignition comes out on ACC position. 

This ignition has no sidebar. Wafers need to be drill in 2 points. 

Needed replacement because customer’s ignition been damaged with a screw driver. 

First remove the Immo ring by removing one Philips screw at the back of the ring. Impact long extension might be needed. See image for access. 

Set Immo ring aside. 

Drill on both edges of keyway - imagine if you insert the key wafers will pop up and down on both side where the key cuts hit it, so simply destroy the parts of the wafers that pop out. 

You can put some wafers in the new ignition to work with the old key. Put only a few as the key is worn out and wouldn’t operate smoothly with all new wafers. 

Wafers are numbered 1-5. This doesn’t represent the depth so you’ll need to simply insert one spring and one wafer at a time and check with the key.
6.5 cm down and then 2 cm right. Drilling point. Stack-on Safe.

1999 Pontiac Firebird - Remote onboard programming

1. Remove the radio fuse, fuse #17

2. Cycle the ignition switch from OFF to ON 3 times within 5 seconds. BCM enters programming mode by cycling the door locks and activating the hatch release.

3. Depress and hold both the lock and unlock buttons on the first remote for up to 16 seconds. The door locks and the hatch release will lock and unlock to indicate that the remote been recognized. 

4. Release the buttons on the remote, but do not proceed further until the locks have finished cycling.

5. Additional remotes can be added by repeating step three above for each remote.

6. Turning the ignition off and putting the fuse back will end programming mode.

Passlock ignition programming:

1. Turn ignition on.
2. Attempt to start the engine, and then release the key to the “ON” position.
3. Observe the “SECURITY” indicator light. After 10 minutes the “SECURITY” indicator light will turn off.
4. Turn ignition to the “OFF” position, and wait 10 seconds.
5. Attempt to start the engine, and then release the key to the “ON” position.
6. Observe the “SECURITY” indicator light. After 10 minutes the “SECURITY” indicator light will turn off.
7. Turn ignition to the “OFF” position, and wait 10 seconds.
8. Attempt to start the engine, and then release the key to the “ON” position.
9. Observe the “SECURITY” indicator light. After 10 minutes the “SECURITY” indicator light will turn off.
10. Turn ignition to the “OFF” position, and wait 10 seconds.
11. Vehicle has now learned the new password. Start the engine.
12. With a scan tool, clear any trouble codes.

NOTE: For most cars, one 10-minute cycle will be enough for the vehicle to learn the new password. Perform all 3 cycles if the car will not start after 1 cycle. Most trucks will require all 3 cycles for learning the password

2016 Chevy Silverado - Ignition repair.
Key won’t turn in ign.

This require the special GM V2 green ignition removal tool, didn’t carry it, did without it. 

Remove clam shell
(No screws)
Bump working key to turn
Standard retainer pin on top 
Ign comes off in START position 

BEWARE - slide it out SLOW observe and preserve the retainer or it’ll go flying. 

To access tumblers need to remove ignition cylinder sleeve 

After ignition cylinder in your hand you’ll need to free up the sleeve from the actual cylinder. Simply slide it out towards the tailpiece end (without key in cylinder) and while you do that press each biding tumbler with a straight ice pick. 

Leave 3-4 tumblers 
Throw away the rest 

The tumblers you leave - file off their heads down a little for smooth operation. 

Reinstallation:
Must remove the tailpiece part from inside the housing - yep, it stays there after you remove the cylinder. 

To do it you’d need to use two ice picks. One hook to pull on the tailpiece part, and one 35/90 degree to depress the white buzzer springy pin inside the housing. 

Then assemble the ignition cylinder with the tailpiece part.

Then put ignition housing in ON position
Reinsert the full cylinder assembly. 
Tip: play with the “sleeve” part rotation as needed to slide the cylinder fully back in the housing.

Once you have a working key for thde doors do this:

1. Remove the key lock cylinder cap. Insert the vehicle key into the key lock cylinder on the driver door handle; then turn the key counterclockwise, to the unlock position five times within 10 seconds.The Driver Information Center(DIC) displays REMOTE LEARN PENDING, PLEASE WAIT.
 
2. Wait for 10 minutes until the DIC displays PRESS ENGINE START BUTTON TO LEARN, then press the ENGINE START/STOP button. (You may have to open and close drivers door to see the DIC display). The DIC display will again show REMOTE LEARN PENDING, PLEASE WAIT.
 
3. Repeat Step 2 two additional times. After the third time all previously known transmitters will no longer work with the vehicle. The DIC displays PRESS ENGINE START BUTTON TO LEARN, then press the ENGINE START/STOP button. (You may have to open and close drivers door to see the DIC display). Remaining transmitters can be relearned during the next steps. The DIC display should now show READY FOR REMOTE # 1.
 
4. Place the new transmitter in the transmitter pocket with buttons facing the rear of the vehicle. The transmitter pocket is inside the center console storage area between the driver and front passenger seats. The storage area will need to be opened to access the transmitter pocket.
 
5. Press the ENGINE START/STOP button. When the transmitter is learned, the DIC display will show that it is ready to program the next transmitter.

6. Remove the transmitter from the transmitter pocket and press unlock or lock on the transmitter.
 
To program additional transmitters, repeat Steps 4–6. When all additional transmitters are  programmed, press and hold the ENGINE START/STOP button for approximately 12  seconds to exit programming mode.

Programming Notes:
This procedure will erase all previously programmed remotes. You must program all existing and new remotes that you wish to use on the vehicle at this time.

1. CLOSE all doors.

2. INSERT key into the ignition.

3. PRESS and HOLD the power UNLOCK button on driver’s side door panel. DO NOT release until instructed to do so in Step 5.

4. Quickly TURN the Ignition ON, OFF, ON, OFF. (ON is the position just shy of starting your vehicle, OFF is the position where you can remove your key)

5. RELEASE the power UNLOCK button on the Driver’s side door panel. The vehicle should respond by locking and unlocking automatically. (A) If locks cycle then CONTINUE to Step 6. (B) If the door locks begin to LOCK and UNLOCK BEFORE releasing the unlock button then the vehicle has not entered Programming Mode and you must START OVER. REMOVE key, OPEN door and RETURN to Step 1. (C) If the vehicle continues to LOCK and UNLOCK before releasing the UNLOCK button then there is a problem with the vehicle’s system and remotes must be programmed by a certified professional. If you are unable to get the door locks to cycle then you are turning the key too quick, too slow, there’s a problem with the vehicle’s system, or the vehicle is not equipped with a factory keyless entry system.

6. HOLD the LOCK and UNLOCK buttons on the remote at the same time until door locks cycle again. This could take up to 30 seconds.

7. Now REPEAT Step 6 for all additional remotes to be programmed,  including working ones.

8. After Step 6 has been performed for all remotes TURN ignition to ON to exit programming mode.

9. TURN ignition to OFF, and remove key.

10. Test all remotes. Programming is complete.

2016 2017 Hyundai Sonata - Trunk lockout

Defective trunk latch. Moderate-hard labor job. 
No less than 250ish keep

Also ensure cust aware there will be minimal damage that is completely harmless to the car and invisible after all components are reassembled upon completion of the work. 
If customer is too entitled / thinks it can be opened is some other magical way - refuse the job. 

Symptom is trunk won’t unlock with any of these methods: manual key, trunk unlock button in car, trunk unlock button on fob. 

Only way to unlock the car is to fold the rear driver side seat.

To do this you must fold down the rear cup holder shelf, then use lot of force to create the widest possible gap (use huge flat head / hammer for shimming & prying), then  identify and push the seat folding lever towards the back of the car with a long reach tool and a flashlight. 

The rear passenger seat folding lever is located inside the truck behind the rear passenger seat itself (top right if you look at the trunk from inside the car). 

Then the rear driver side seat will fold (fold it while pressing on the release lever with the long reach tool). 

From here, it’s easy to reach the rear passenger side seat folding lever (in the trunk) as well, same place just behind the rear passenger side seat.

Once both seats are folded, easily reach the defective latch by crawling into the trunk, and dismantle/break the plastic coating of the latch to pieces with a flat head, and move around its guts while someone outside tries to press on the truck release button / turn the cylinder repeatedly. 

That trunk latch can be easily replaced. Roughly $30 part

(suppose to be the same for 2003 and 2005)

Was manual gear.

MAZ24 lishi, MZ31 test, only H92 worked. 
MAZ34 2-3 keys failed.

Tricky car - it has 2 types of ECU (see images below)
To identify ecu type look at the large connector at the bottom of the ecu. 

Ecu can easily be found around driver’s left knee area.
Our ecu was like type 1. 

*Note type 1 can not be done by EEPROM (no info available). 

*Type 2 can easily be done by EEPROM, 8 leg 24C02 out of circuit. 

The only chip that we were able to program to this car was from H92 Ford key that we put next to a metal key, we selected AKL with IM100 and programmed two H92.

MAZ34 2-3 different keys failed to learn including with SP

Mazda OEM Lucas key failed to learn including with SP

For ecu type 1 we could not find any Eeprom information, nor could we find any identifiable 8 leg device on this ECU.

Please note, since H92 cannot be easily open, Matt ended up cloning out the H92s to two other super chips (no sniffing required).

Conclusions 
1. Possibly required 4D63 OEM chip (we were not sure if the H92s that Matt used had OEM chip inside)
2. Small chance but possible that the MAZ34 chips were defective.

Removing the black plastic cover above driver’s legs by removing 1 Star screw above driver’s leg, now pull down on the black cover’s edge that’s closer to you and pop (downwards) 2 clicks for 2 clips. Disconnect 2 wire connections OBD and another small wire next to OBD. 
Now carefully slid the black plastic cover out towards you and set it aside. 

Above driver’s right leg is the Kessey module hidden in its bracket. Remove 1 zip tie locking it to the bracket. Now press on the bracket’s clip to slide out the Kessey. Kessey has 2 connections one round looking and one rectangle. Carefully remove the round first using a small flat head. Now in the back (far) side of the rectangle connector there is a grey slider that needs to be pushed (slide) away from the connector, simply slide it away using the same small flat head and carefully remove the connector. Blow heat It out of circuit 
Soldier it to VVprog’s green adaptor. 1st leg (ST logo) by dot of first leg. 

Go to the laptop - VVDI Prog - EEPROM - ST - M93C86 - Read - save file. 

Go to VV2 - transponder Programmer - immo data tool - Euro - Porsche - Kessey 

Press ‘load DUMP file’ and load the file you saved earlier, you’ll now see how many keys are on the device - insert Porsche key to VV2 (car shape headlight head first) - now select ‘Make Dealer Key’ - you’ll get success message - press ok - it’ll prompt you to save the DUMP file - save the DUMP file.

Now go back to VVprog
Press ‘load’ top left - choose the DUMP file - press ‘write’ to write it into the 93C86 - when successful you are done. Soldier the 93C86 back to the Kessey. Cut key be Lishi (must choose by Porsche by model to get the ‘extra cut’), connect back the 2 connectors and start the car. Keep in mind, When inserting a programmed key just by inserting dash should turn on after 2-5 seconds.

First of all we need the 8 digit ID code that is either on the fob's bag, or somewhere inside the board's circuit (Need to open the fob)

1. All doors closed
Within 45 seconds:
2. Open, close driver's door twice
3. Ignition key ON-OFF 10 times - A tone/buzzer will indicate programming mode started.
4. FAST On the remote press lock as many times as the leftmost/first number on the ID code we got before. Then hold the unlock button.
Repeat 7 more times for the other 7 numbers
5. FAST Repeat last step. All 8 numbers, a second time.

To exit programming mode remove key from ign

How to cut Subaru high security single sided Ekey / Eblade / emergency key:

Getting cuts options:
Lishi, side screw + read stamped letters on wafers, buy code. 

We bought code from Discount. 
Code comes like this: 
Cuts: 31234432
Code: 94572

(Lockcodes & Instacode couldn’t translate the key code, no need though, it comes with bitting s as you can see). 

The trick! Insert the bitting in S9 from right to left: 
If cuts are 31234432 per code, 
You’d insert:
(A) 2344
(B) 3213

Done.

Alternative ways:
See images to dismantle door lock & remove wafers, then read the stamped letters on them. 
“i” represents depth 1
“N” represents depth 2 
“S” represents depth 3
“Y” represents depth 4

Order of tumblers inside the code from closest to keyway to furthest from keyway: A1,B1,A2,B2,A3,B3,A4,B4

Remember you’d first read all A row (A1-A4) stamped letters and insert them first in A row on S9
Then read all B row (B1-B4) stamped letters and insert their corresponding depth value in S9 for B row.

2002 Lexus RX300 - Ignition repair job. Ignition on dash. 
(It’s a reflash job if AKL). 
Customer complained he couldn’t turn the key in the ignition. 

Sergey arrived and ensured the cylinder does not have binding tumblers. (Regular Toyota / Lexus ignition repair). 

Still ignition won’t turn. Sergey found out that the male tailpiece inside the housing won’t even turn with needle nose pliers.

We sold an ignition housing replacement for about $950. 
(Ignition switch assembly).

We ordered a housing from ebay for a 2001 Lexus GS300, description said it fits our 2002 RX300 ($70).

On site Roman identified this housing was NOT correct. 
See images for the correct housing for this model. 

Upon further investigation on site we discovered the issue. 
The male interior tailpiece (which is part of the housing) can only turn if you slightly press it in before you try to turn. 

It actually even says on the ignition face cap “push” with a direction arrow for turning. 

It turns out the customer’s key had a bunch of tape on it where the blade meets the bow of the key - that technically prevented the extra slight “push” on the key into the core (plug) thus pressing the core (plug) inwards a little which then slightly presses the interior male tailpiece in so twisting motion is enabled. 

Moral of story - solution was to simply produce a replacement key (without the tape on it.)

We programmed that replacement key onboard.

2002 Toyota Camry - remote programming. (This procedure is used on many Toyota vehicles)

1. All doors closed, driver’s door opened and unlocked, key out of the ignition.

2. Insert and remove the key in the ignition two times within five seconds. Do not turn the key in the ignition.

3. Close and open the driver’s door twice within 40 seconds.

4. Insert key in the ignition and remove it. (Do not turn it.)

5. Close and open the driver’s door twice within 40 seconds.

6. Insert the key into the ignition. (Do not turn it.)

7. Close the driver’s door.

8. Turn the key in the ignition from OFF to ON and then back to OFF at about one second intervals to select the desired function – see below.

One time for add mode - to add a remote without erasing any previously programmed remotes

Two times for rewrite mode - to add a remote and erase all previously programmed remotes

Three times for confirmation mode - to see how many remotes are currently programmed.

9. Remove the key from the ignition.

10. To confirm your mode selection, the power door locks will cycle from lock to unlock the same number of times that you turned the key in the ignition. Note: If confirmation mode or prohibition mode has been selected, opening the door will complete the procedure.

11. For the add or rewrite modes, within 40 seconds of power door lock confirmation:

12. Simultaneously press the lock and unlock buttons on the remote for one to one and a half seconds and release.

13. Within three seconds of step A, press the lock button on the remote for more than one second and then release.

14. If the remote has been successfully programmed, the power door locks will cycle once at this time. If there are problems with the remote transmitter or the procedure up to this point the power door locks will cycle twice. 
If this happens, verify that you have the proper remote and then repeat the procedure.

15. If additional remotes are to be programmed repeat steps A – C above.

16. Opening the driver’s door will end the procedure.

8. CLOSE the DRIVER's door.

TWICE - erase all remotes and reprogram existing remotes

13. The door locks will cycle to confirm successful programming of the remote. 

*If you have any additional remotes to program repeat step 12 if you have no additional remotes proceed to step 14.

14. OPEN the DRIVER'S door to exit programming mode and then test the remote.

👁🔔 Disable Active Alarm on New Platform Toyota BZX4 and Tundra

Here is how to deactivate an active alarm:

⿡ Cut an E key for the vehicle, and you should close all doors, trunk/hatch, and hood.

⿢ Wait for the alarm to stop sounding; it usually takes about 60 seconds to stop sounding. (If the alarm is sounding, this process will not work.)

⿣ Insert the E key into the driver’s door lock and turn it in the following sequence: Left, Left, Right, Left, Right, Left, Right. (This must be done before the alarm goes off.)

⿤ You must cycle the key in this sequence before the alarm goes off, or it will not work.

The alarm will be deactivated. You can then open the door.

column1: How to recognize Master key for Lexus & Toyota models
column16:
How to recognize Master key for Lexus & Toyota models: 

‘Master’ key - when inserted into the ignition lock cylinder will cause the Security light to stay out, not illuminated. Some Master keys are stored or recognized as Valet keys. This happens in less than 5% of the Lexus & Toyota models on the road. If the vehicle does not recognize a Master key, additional keys cannot be added without a immobilizer reset or ECU re-flash.

‘Valet’ key - when inserted into the ignition lock cylinder will cause the Security light to stay ON for 1 to 2 seconds and then stay out, not illuminated. Valet keys cannot be used to add additional keys, whether Master or Valet.

1. Key out of the ignition

14. OPEN the DRIVER'S door to exit programming mode and then test the remote.

Step 2:‭ ‭ ‭ ‬Enter 8-8-8 followed by the # button. The lock will beep 2 times.‬‬
Step 3:‭ ‭ ‬Enter the Current Master Code followed by the # button. ‬
The lock will beep 2 times.
Step 4:‭ ‭ ‬Enter a New Master Code followed by the # button. ‬
The lock will beep 2 times.
Step 5:‭ ‭ ‬Re-enter the New Master Code followed by the # button. ‬
The light will stay green for 3 seconds.

- ‭/ 8-8-8-# /‬ Master Code-# ‭/‬ New Master Code-# ‭/‬ New Master Code-#‭ ‬
